excerpt: TinyFolder adds custom app folders to the Mac Dock: one click opens a folder of apps above its tile. Free plan, Pro prices on the website and App Store, and alternatives.
content:
TinyFolder is a Mac app that adds app folders to the Dock, something the Mac Dock can't do on its own. You pick a set of apps, pin the folder, and one click opens it right above its Dock tile. The folder's icon is built from the apps inside, so you can see what it holds at a glance.

Most of the app is about design. A live editor lets you choose glass, colour or texture, icon, list or large-tile layouts, icon size, labels and living effects such as snow and drifting light, with 64 built-in presets. Each folder can also have its own keyboard shortcut. TinyFolder launches apps only: you can't drop files onto the apps inside a folder, and apps that are running still appear in the Dock, as macOS requires.

There are two editions. The Mac App Store version is limited to one folder in the Dock, because App Store rules only let an app change its own Dock icon. The version downloaded from tinyfolder.app can pin as many folders as you like. TinyFolder is designed and built by Sergey Filkov and launched on Product Hunt on 4 October 2026, finishing #16 for the day with 75 upvotes.

We have not tested TinyFolder ourselves. This page brings together its official site, its Mac App Store listing, its Product Hunt page and the official pages of comparable apps, and says where each fact comes from.

profile.os: Direct download: macOS 13 or later, Apple silicon and Intel. App Store: macOS 13.1 or later, Apple silicon
profile.starts_at: Free (1 folder); Lifetime Pro $21 on the website
profile.summary_short: Mac app that adds custom, designable app folders to the Dock
use_cases: Grouping apps you use once a week into one Dock folder to keep the Dock short
Replacing Launchpad, which macOS Tahoe removed, with folders you design
Opening a group of work apps with a keyboard shortcut

paragraphs: Sergey Filkov says his Dock kept growing, with apps he opens once a week sitting next to the ones he uses all day. On an iPhone you would make a folder, but the Mac Dock can't. The nearest option was a stack of aliases next to the Trash, and with macOS Tahoe even Launchpad was gone.

So he built TinyFolder: pick your apps, pin the folder, and one click opens it above the tile. He explained the one constraint up front: the App Store sandbox only lets an app change its own Dock icon, so the App Store version gives you one folder, while the version from tinyfolder.app pins as many as you like. It is free to start, needs no account and works offline.
launch_story.attribution: Sergey Filkov, maker, on Product Hunt

fit: have a crowded Dock and want folders like on an iPhone
miss Launchpad after upgrading to macOS Tahoe
like to customise how your Mac looks
not_fit: want several folders from the Mac App Store version: it allows one; use the direct download instead
want a launcher for files and documents: TinyFolder opens apps only
use an Intel Mac and want the App Store edition: that one is Apple silicon only

pricing.intro: TinyFolder is free to start. Pro prices differ between the version sold on its website and the Mac App Store version. Prices are in US dollars.

plans.name: Starter
plans.detail: 1 folder with up to 4 apps, Liquid Glass style, pin to Dock, no account, no time limit

plans.name: Lifetime Pro, 2 Macs (website)
plans.detail: Unlimited folders and apps, the full design studio, 64 presets, 4 icon packs, global shortcuts and future updates. 7-day money-back guarantee

plans.name: Yearly Pro (App Store)
plans.detail: In-app purchase in the Mac App Store edition, which is limited to one Dock folder

plans.name: Lifetime Pro (App Store)
plans.detail: In-app purchase in the Mac App Store edition; includes every style pack. Style packs are also sold separately at $4.99 each

notes: The website's $21 price is a launch deal "while the launch price lasts".
Website purchases are processed by Paddle; you activate the licence with your email and key. App Store purchases and refunds go through Apple.
App Store prices are the US prices shown on 14 October 2026.

alternatives.intro: From Product Hunt's alternatives list. Prices are what each product's own site or App Store listing states, checked on 14 October 2026. Review scores are Product Hunt users' own.

items.name: DockFix
items.what: Replaces the macOS Dock with a customisable one
items.difference: Replaces the whole Dock. TinyFolder keeps Apple's Dock and adds folders to it.

items.name: Launchie
items.what: Launchpad-style full-screen app grid for macOS 26
items.difference: A full-screen grid opened with a shortcut rather than a folder in the Dock. It needs macOS 26.

items.name: Kickfolder
items.what: Folders, files and apps that slide down from the top edge of the screen
items.difference: Lives at the top edge, including the notch, and handles files too. It needs macOS 26.2 or later.

alternatives.more: Product Hunt also lists Alfred, Docky, DockFlow, LaunchOS, Dockify and Launchy.

pros: Adds real app folders to Apple's own Dock
Free plan with no account and no time limit
Deep visual customisation with a live preview
Website licence covers 2 Macs, with a 7-day money-back guarantee
Works offline; folder contents and styling are never uploaded, according to the privacy policy
cons: The App Store edition allows only one folder in the Dock
Pro prices differ by where you buy it
The App Store edition sends anonymous usage counts unless you switch them off

x.none: We found no posts about TinyFolder on X yet.

faq.a: Yes, for one folder with up to four apps, with no time limit and no account. Pro unlocks unlimited folders and the full design tools.

faq.q: Why does the App Store version allow only one folder?
faq.a: The maker says the App Store sandbox only lets an app change its own Dock icon, so each copy can show one folder. The version from tinyfolder.app can pin as many folders as you like.
On the website, Lifetime Pro for 2 Macs was $21 once on 14 October 2026, a launch price down from $32. In the Mac App Store, Pro is $9.99 a year or $29.99 once.

faq.q: Do running apps still show in the Dock?
faq.a: Yes. macOS shows running apps in the Dock; TinyFolder saves space for the apps that aren't running.
Website purchases have a 7-day, no-questions money-back guarantee. App Store purchases are refunded through Apple.

faq.q: Which Macs does it run on?
faq.a: The direct download needs macOS 13 or later and runs on Apple silicon and Intel. The App Store edition needs macOS 13.1 or later on Apple silicon.
